title: add-benchmark-lab-profiling-baselines-and-representative-workload-runners-reporting-pipeline
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds profiling baselines (seq-len 512/2048), representative workload runners for latency/throughput scenarios, and a nightly reporting pipeline that exports aggregated results to BigQuery. No breaking changes. Improves benchmark reproducibility and adds CI coverage for nightly runs.
description:
Context: This PR centralizes the next iteration of the benchmark lab: we add profiling baselines (multiple sequence lengths and batch profiles), representative workload runners (chat, streaming, embeddings), and a reporting pipeline that aggregates results, computes baselines/regressions, and exports to BigQuery for dashboards. Motivation: enable consistent perf/regression detection across hosted/dedicated/private deployments and automate nightly reporting.

What I changed: - Added profiling baselines under benchmark-lab/profiling/ (yaml + scripts) for seq-len 128/512/2048 and batch sizes representative of production traffic. - Implemented representative runners in benchmark-lab/runners/ to simulate chat, single-turn generation, embeddings, and reranking workloads with realistic token distributions. - New reporting pipeline in benchmark-lab/reporting/ that ingests runner outputs, normalizes metrics, computes deltas vs baselines, and writes summary tables to BigQuery. - CI: added ci/benchmarks.yml job to run a fast smoke of runners on PRs and nightly full-run job. - Docs: updated docs/benchmark-lab/README.md with usage and how to add a new workload.

Commits: Add profiling baselines and loader; Implement representative workload runners and harness; Add reporting pipeline ETL and BigQuery export; Add nightly CI job + smoke PR job; Fix runner shutdown race and logging.

Files changed (high level): benchmark-lab/runners/representative_runners.py, benchmark-lab/profiling/baselines/*.yaml, benchmark-lab/reporting/etl/run_reporting.py, benchmark-lab/reporting/config.yaml, ci/benchmarks.yml, docs/benchmark-lab/README.md, tests/benchmarks/test_runner_smoke.py, infra/terraform/etl_bigquery.tf.

Checklist: - [x] Add baseline data and loader - [x] Add representative runners and unit tests - [x] Add reporting pipeline and BigQuery export - [x] CI smoke + nightly job - [x] Docs updated - [x] Benchmarks ran locally and against staging infra

Impact: This enables automated regression detection and reduces manual effort to produce perf dashboards. No user-facing API changes. Backwards-compatible with existing benchmark data format.

Migration notes: The BigQuery dataset name is parameterized; operators should add credentials/secrets in the infra repo before enabling nightly exports.

Merge: Squash-merged after approvals and green CI.
commit_summary: Implement representative workload runners (chat, single-turn, embeddings, reranking)
Add reporting ETL and BigQuery export + config
Add CI job (ci/benchmarks.yml) for PR smoke and nightly runs
Fix runner shutdown race and add more logging
review_comments: Miguel Torres: Can you split the baseline generator from the runner harness? It makes the smoke tests faster — responded and split into two modules.
Priya Ramesh: Performance numbers look reasonable; please add a regression alert threshold to the reporting pipeline — added a configurable threshold and tests.
Ben Carlson: Minor nits on log formatting, and add a retry on BigQuery insert failures — fixed and added exponential backoff.
Aisha Patel (author): Addressed feedback, split modules, added tests and CI updates. Ready for final reviews.
notes: This PR was coordinated with infra to provision the BigQuery dataset parameter in a follow-up infra-only PR (ENG-7934). Nightly runs are gated behind a feature flag until dataset is configured.
migration_instructions: Operators must provision a BigQuery dataset and add the service account to secrets/benchmark_bigquery_sa in the infra repo. Update benchmark-lab/reporting/config.yaml to point to the dataset. No data migration required for existing baselines.
changelog_entry: benchmark(lab): add profiling baselines, representative workload runners, and nightly reporting pipeline (BigQuery export).
